items.title: George Wein interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: And Wild Bill Davison and a few other guests. We sold out Jordan Hall.

ctx.x: It’s like you were improvising from the moment, every time a moment came up.

I had never been in business. I didn’t know what it was to be in business, I wasn’t a businessman. And I was a graduate, I was playing piano, and somebody says, “Open up a club.” I opened up a club. But I knew everybody in Boston. I knew the whole jazz world. I knew all the radio people, because I’d been playing at clubs all the time. And I’d done one concert with Edmond Hall, it was Edmond Hall and George Wein present, and then Nat Hentoff wrote the liner notes, because he was a Boston D.J. at that time and a…
Well as clubs go, you had a great run. I mean when you think about how quickly some clubs open and close.

items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the first evening that I produced at Newport, I had Eddie Condon with Bobby Hackett and Wild Bill Davison and Pee Wee Russell and a few others

ctx.x: Was that the Brass Bands to BeBop?

Brass Bands to BeBop. Nat Hentoff wrote the album notes and MC'd the program. I brought up Wild Bill Davison and Frankie Newton and J.C. [Higginbotham] from New York, and we sold out Jordan Hall in Boston. Beautiful hall … at the New England Conservatory of Music. I guess that was the first bite of the insect that infected me the rest of my life.

items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: when I went back - I had played for George Wein in Nice

ctx.x: Because I think-- you know, if you go sit and listen to a modern festival - George Wein has put on a modern festival; I heard one once and it's over and over you're hearing the same thing---
Well, a lot of Newport's modern now.
